MARKE.|115}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=10|verse=35}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 20, 20.''}}* there come to him Iames and Iohn the {{ls}}onnes of Zebedee, {{ls}}aying, Mai{{ls}}ter, vve vvil that vvhat thing {{ls}}oeuer vve {{ls}}hal a{{ls}}ke, thou doe it to vs. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=36}}† But he {{ls}}aid to them, What vvil you that I doe to you? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=37}}† And they {{ls}}aid, Graunt to vs, that vve may {{ls}}it, one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left hand, in thy glorie. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=38}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aid to them, You vvotte not vvhat you a{{ls}}ke. can you drinke the cuppe that I drinke: or be baptized vvith the bapti{{ls}}me vvhervvith I am baptized? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=39}}† But they {{ls}}aid to him, VVe can. And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aid to them, The cuppe in deede vvhich I drinke, you {{ls}}hal drinke: and vvith the bapti{{ls}}me vvhervvith I am baptized, {{ls}}hal you be baptized: {{verse|chapter=10|verse=40}}† but to {{ls}}it on my right hand or on my left, is not mine to giue vnto you, but to vvhom it is prepared. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=41}}† And the ten hearing, began to be di{{ls}}plea{{ls}}ed at Iames and Iohn. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=42}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} calling them, {{ls}}aith to them, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 20, 25. Lu. 22, 25.''}}* You knovv that they vvhich {{ls}}eeme to rule ouer the gentiles, ouerrule them: and their Princes haue povver ouer them. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=43}}† But it is not {{ls}}o in you. but vvho{{ls}}oeuer vvil be greater, {{ls}}hal be your mini{{ls}}ter: {{verse|chapter=10|verse=44}}† and vvho{{ls}}oeuer vvil be fir{{ls}}t among you, {{ls}}hal be the {{ls}}eruant of al. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=45}}† For the Sonne of man al{{ls}}o is not come to be mini{{ls}}tred vnto, but to mini{{ls}}ter, and to giue his life a redempption for many. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=46}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 20, 29. Lu. 18, 35.''}}* they come to Iericho: and vvhen he departed from Iericho, and his Di{{ls}}ciples, and a very great multitude, the {{ls}}onne of Timæus, Bar-timæus the blinde man, {{ls}}ate by the way {{ls}}ide begging. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=47}}† VVho vvhen he had heard, that it is {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth: he began to crie, and to {{ls}}ay, {{sc|Iesvs}}, {{ls}}onne of Dauid, haue mercie vpon me. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=48}}† And many threatened him, to hold his peace. but he cried much more, Sonne of Dauid, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=49}}† haue mercie vpon me. And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}tanding {{ls}}til commaunded him to be called. And they call the blinde man, {{ls}}aying to him, Be of better comfort, ari{{ls}}e, he calleth thee. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=50}}† VVho ca{{ls}}ting of his garment leapt vp, and came to him. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=51}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} an{{ls}}vvering, {{ls}}aid to him, VVhat vvilt thou that I doe vnto thee? And the blinde man {{ls}}aid to him, Rabbôni, that I may {{ls}}ee. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=52}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} {{ls}}aid to him, Goe thy vvaies, thy faith hath made the {{ls}}afe. And forthvvith he {{ls}}avv, and folovved him in the vvay.<noinclude>{{rh||P ij|ANNOT}}</noinclude>
